Configure when the app starts automatically

This device may require enabling auto-start and removing battery optimization or background restrictions for this app.\n\nOn head units with Quick Boot (fast boot), auto-start may not work. Look for \"DuraSpeed\" in your system settings and enable this app there. On some head units, DuraSpeed is hidden and you may need an app like \"Hidden Settings\" to find it. If you don\'t have DuraSpeed, try disabling Quick Boot.
Open the app automatically when the device starts up. Requires \'Display over other apps\' permission on Android 10+

Open the app every time the screen turns on. Ideal for head units that never fully shut down or use fast boot modes where the other auto-start options don\'t work. Not recommended for phones or tablets.
Automatically open Open Headunit when connected to a specific WiFi SSID.
Connect only when connected to this WiFi SSID
Legacy Feature: This may not work reliably on Android 8+ due to background restrictions. Ensure the app is excluded from battery optimization.
Bluetooth permission is required to select paired devices. Please grant it in app settings.
To allow Open Headunit to open automatically when Bluetooth connects, please enable the "Display over other apps" permission in the next screen.

Configure auto-connect methods and their priority order
These methods run automatically when the app opens. Enable the ones you want, then drag to set the order. The first enabled method that succeeds will be used.
Ignores aspect ratio to fill the entire display (removes black bars)
Corrects scaling issues on some older devices using SurfaceView. Only use if the image looks distorted or shifted.
Flips the display horizontally for windshield reflection (Head-Up Display). Requires TextureView or GLES20 view mode (does not work with SurfaceView).
Normalize touch input against the measured projection overlay. May help when small Android Auto controls feel shifted.
If disabled, the headunit will not receive audio. Sound will play from the phone.
Force the phone to believe audio focus is always held, preventing audio routing losses on generic headunits. Also performs software ducking during navigation voice prompts.
Separate audio channels for music, calls, and notifications instead of a single multimedia stream (may not work correctly on some devices).
Use AAC codec for audio to save bandwidth (Experimental).

Attaches a dummy Equalizer effect to the audio session to force hardware DSP routing on specific headunits. Keep disabled if using ViPER4Android / ViperFX or if sound is muffled on older Android versions.
Configure microphone input and audio processing.
Choose the audio source for the microphone.
Attempts to remove echo from the microphone. Disable if you experience silence or distortion.
Attempts to reduce background noise. Disable if your voice sounds muffled.
Automatically adjusts microphone volume. Disable if the volume is unstable.

Get more information about Open Headunit
Search or report bugs on GitHub

If you run into a bug or a problem, please first look for it in the GitHub issues list. If no one has reported it yet, open a new issue and describe what happens, your head unit, and the steps to reproduce it.
Or scan this QR code to open the issues list on another device.
Note: you need a free GitHub account to create an issue.
Only two things are required. Everything else is optional, but it helps solve your problem much faster.

Please always write your issue in English. It is the one language the maintainer and most people helping here share, and a thread in many languages just turns into a little Tower of Babel where nobody can help anyone. No one judges you, your level of English or the way you write, so do not worry about mistakes. If it helps, a translator like Google Translate or DeepL, or an AI like ChatGPT or Claude, can write and tidy up your message in English for you.
The Android version of the device projecting Android Auto (your head unit or screen), and its brand and model if you know them.
USB cable, USB wireless adapter, WiFi Direct, WiFi (headunit server) or Self Mode. If it is wireless, add the adapter or dongle model.
The Open Headunit version, shown on the About screen.
Attach logs, right after it happens

Switch Settings to the Advanced tab, turn on Debug Mode in the Debug section, reproduce the problem, then tap Export Logs right after so the log covers the moment it broke and not just the start. Attach that file to your issue.
First search the existing issues. If an open issue already describes your problem, add your details as a comment there instead of opening a new one. Only open a new issue if none matches.
Your phone model, its Android version and the Android Auto app version on the phone. Some problems come from a specific Android Auto release.
What you did, what you expected and what actually happened. A screenshot or a short video helps a lot for visual problems.
Keep each issue to a single problem so it can be tracked and fixed. Open separate issues for unrelated problems.

Automatically close the app when Android Auto disconnects

The following reconnection settings will conflict with closing the app on disconnect:

%1$s

Your initial connection settings (auto-connect, auto-start) will still work when the headunit turns on. However, after the first disconnection the app will close immediately instead of trying to reconnect.

Note: Some aftermarket head units never fully shut down — they hibernate instead, similar to a phone that locks its screen but never actually powers off. With this option enabled, the app will close after the first disconnection and may not reopen automatically on the next ignition cycle.

Would you like to disable the reconnection settings listed above?

You have \"Start on boot\" enabled. If the app closes on disconnect and this device hibernates instead of shutting down, the app may not reopen automatically on the next ignition cycle because no boot event is triggered — the device simply wakes up from sleep.

You have \"Start on screen on\" enabled. This setting opens the app every time the screen turns on. Combined with closing on disconnect, the app will close after disconnection but reopen immediately when the screen turns on again, creating a restart loop.

Wait for WiFi before WiFi Direct
On boot, wait for WiFi to connect before starting WiFi Direct. Enable this if your head unit needs a few seconds to connect to WiFi after power on.
Note: Wireless Android Auto on 2.4GHz devices can lead to lag, stutters, and disconnects. If you experience issues, please test via USB to confirm if it\'s a network limitation.

Our name is changing to Open Headunit

Headunit Revived is growing, thanks to you, and it is turning into something of its own: Open Headunit. We are rolling the new name out over the next updates, so you may still see the old name in some places for a while.\n\nSame app, same people behind it, and all your settings stay exactly as they are.
